definitions.gloss: luxury item; luxury goods; non-essential item
definitions.explanation: An expensive or extravagant item that is not a necessity but a desirable indulgence. Contrasted with daily necessities.

examples.japanese: {贅沢品|ぜいたくひん}は{買|か}わないようにしている。
examples.english: I try not to buy luxury items.

examples.japanese: ブランドバッグは{贅沢品|ぜいたくひん}だと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think brand-name bags are luxury goods.

examples.japanese: {戦時中|せんじちゅう}は{贅沢品|ぜいたくひん}の{販売|はんばい}が{制限|せいげん}され、{生活|せいかつ}{必需品|ひつじゅひん}だけが{手|て}に{入|はい}った。
examples.english: During wartime, the sale of luxury goods was restricted, and only daily necessities were available.

notes:
{贅沢品|ぜいたくひん} is a compound of {贅沢|ぜいたく} (luxury, extravagance) + {品|ひん} (goods). It refers to non-essential, expensive items — things you want but don't need.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {贅沢品|ぜいたくひん}を{買|か}う (to buy luxury goods)
- {贅沢品|ぜいたくひん}に{税金|ぜいきん}をかける (to tax luxury goods)
- {贅沢品|ぜいたくひん}と{必需品|ひつじゅひん} (luxuries and necessities)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {必需品|ひつじゅひん}: necessities, essential goods
- {日用品|にちようひん}: daily goods, everyday items
- {高級品|こうきゅうひん}: high-quality goods (emphasizes quality, not extravagance)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Historically, {贅沢|ぜいたく}は{敵|てき}だ (luxury is the enemy) was a wartime slogan. The concept of restraining luxury spending has deep roots in Japanese culture.
